record.what_it_does: Slack is a business messaging platform, and its developer platform lets apps read, write, and automate messages, channels, users, and workspace data via APIs.
record.auth_notes: OAuth2 (v2) is the standard flow for apps installed across multiple workspaces, producing bot (xoxb) and/or user (xoxp) tokens. A single-workspace ('undistributed') app can skip the OAuth redirect flow entirely and get a bot token directly via a one-click 'Install App to Workspace' button, which then functions as a static bearer token sent in the Authorization header.
record.access_notes: Anyone can sign up for Slack free, create an app at api.slack.com/apps, and install it to their own workspace immediately to get a working access token at no cost. For a multi-workspace/multi-tenant agent toolkit, an app can enable 'Activate Public Distribution' (unlisted distribution) self-serve, with no Slack review, to install via OAuth into any workspace. Only submitting to the Slack Marketplace directory (optional, for commercial discoverability) requires a formal review (preliminary + functional review, up to ~10 weeks) and a minimum install count.
